intro: Games travel. Long ago, people in Mexico bounced rubber balls on stone courts. People in China kicked a leather ball. Native nations of North America played lacrosse. Later, ships and teachers carried soccer, basketball and baseball to new lands.
Some sports need a very different room. Wrestlers use a padded mat. Boxers use a roped square. Fencers use a long, thin strip. Judo began on straw mats at a school in Tokyo in 1882.
In this unit you will learn where games began and how they moved. You will name the room each sport needs. You will put real dates in order.
bigQuestion: How do games move to new places, and why does each sport need its own room?

timeline.t: Wrestling joins the old Olympic Games at Olympia, by tradition
The Football Association forms in London on 26 October
The Queensberry Rules for boxing are printed in England
Horace Wilson teaches baseball to students in Tokyo
Kano Jigoro opens the Kodokan judo school in Tokyo
James Naismith makes basketball at a YMCA school in Springfield
Charles Miller brings two soccer balls and a rule book home to Brazil
The Illinois High School Association begins
FIFA is founded in Paris on 21 May
The IHSA crowns its first boys wrestling state champions
Judo joins the Olympic Games in Tokyo
The IHSA holds its first girls wrestling state finals

test.q: Where did people play with rubber balls on stone courts long ago?
test.why: People in Mexico and Central America played on stone ball courts over 3,000 years ago.
Native nations such as the Haudenosaunee played it long before Europeans came.

test.q: What group formed in London on 26 October 1863?
test.why: Club leaders formed the Football Association to share one set of rules.

test.q: Who took Naismith's game to other gyms?
test.why: Naismith taught at a YMCA school, and YMCA teachers spread basketball.

test.q: Which city's baseball players sailed around the world in 1888?
test.why: Albert Spalding led a world tour with Chicago baseball players.

test.q: What shape is a boxing ring?
test.why: A boxing ring is a roped square, as the Queensberry Rules describe.

test.q: Which sport uses a round clay ring called a dohyo?
test.why: Sumo wrestlers in Japan meet in a dohyo.

test.q: When did Kano open the Kodokan in Tokyo?
test.why: Kano opened the Kodokan judo school in 1882.

test.q: Where was the first World Cup held in 1930?
test.why: Uruguay held and won the first World Cup.

test.q: When did the IHSA hold its first girls wrestling state finals?
test.why: IHSA records show the first girls state finals in 2022.

write.prompt: Pick one game or sport from this unit. Tell where it began and give one date. Then name the room it needs. Use a record from the unit, like the Football Association of 1863 or the Queensberry Rules of 1867.
tips: Say the place where the game began.
Write one real date from the unit.
Name the room: court, field, mat, ring, strip or dohyo.
Name one person or group, like Naismith, Kano or FIFA.
